chunks: Ibn al-Mutawakkil, from Ali, from his father, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, from Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from his forefathers, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Majestic is His Majesty, said: He has not believed in Me the one who interprets My words based on his opinion.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.جَلَّ جَلَالُهُ: Majestic is His Majesty (a divine attribute/title)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to interpret God's words based on one's own opinion in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Imam Ali al-Rida, underscores the Shia scholarly caution against *ra'y* (subjective personal opinion) in Quranic exegesis, distinguishing it from reasoned interpretation (*ijtihad*) grounded in divine guidance. It serves as a foundational text for the principle that true faith (*iman*) is compromised when individuals rely solely on their limited intellect to interpret God's words without the anchor of prophetic and imamic authority. This warning highlights the danger of subjective relativism in theology, a key concern in Shia usul al-fiqh.

en.ammaar-muslim: 4. [4/-] al-Tawhid and al-Uyun and al-Amali: Ibn al-Mutawakkil from Ali from his father from al-Rayyan b. al-Salt from Ali b. Musa al-Ridha from his forefathers from the commander of the faithful عليهم السلام who said:
the messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه واله said: Allah Majestic is His Majesty said: he has not believed in Me the one who interprets My words based on his opinion …
